title: Console walkthrough  usage analytics & cost breakdown (Sunrise Retail)
summary: Redwood AE + SE walked Sunrise Retail through the Console usage analytics and per-route dashboards with emphasis on cost attribution and options for dedicated capacity. Customer is evaluating cost/latency tradeoffs and requested benchmarking and security docs.
next_steps: Jordan: send tailored pricing + dedicated sizing spreadsheet by 2026-12-14
Priya: schedule a 2-hour pilot benchmarking session (throughput/latency) with Lucas w/c 2026-12-21
Marta: share a list of top 10 prompt routes and monthly token estimates
action_items: Jordan Lee - Send pricing deck + dedicated sizing spreadsheet - due 2026-12-14
Priya Singh - Setup pilot benchmark run and provide test plan - due 2026-12-18

transcript:
Header: 2026-12-10 09:00 PT | Duration: 48m
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Singh (Redwood SE), Marta Ruiz (Sunrise), Ethan Park (Sunrise), Lucas Chen (Sunrise)

00:00 Jordan: All right hi everyone, thanks for joining. i'm Jordan with Redwood, i'll run the intro and then Priya will jump into the console walkthrough. can you quick confirm audio?
00:12 Marta: Yep hear you, thanks.
00:15 Ethan: Good to go.
00:18 Jordan: Awesome. Quick agenda  1) Console usage analytics and per-route dashboards, 2) cost breakdown and routing policies, 3) Q&A and next steps. Priya, over to you.
00:31 Priya: Great thanks Jordan. i'll share my screen  tell me if the deck comes up, okay? (screen share) cool. so starting at the console home, you'll see your usage heatmap, token consumption over time and a breakdown by route. this is the per-route dashboard we mentioned in the email.
00:52 Priya: (narrating) here's a sample from a retail customer, you can filter by model, environment (hosted vs dedicated), and time range. the interesting thing is we show per-route p50/p95 latency, tokens in/out, and also cost attribution by route.
01:10 Lucas: sorry quick q  cost attribution is based on model unit cost + token counts only, or does it include infra (gpu) amortization?
01:18 Priya: good question. right now the UI cost breakdown includes model unit costs and inference runtime token billing; for Dedicated we add an amortized capacity line item if you upload reserved pricing. you can toggle to show raw token spend versus total unit economics. note that infra breakdowns are approximate unless you input your committed capacity details.
01:36 Marta: ok so if we go dedicated later we can see a per-route view that includes reserved capacity amortization?
01:41 Priya: yes  you can upload your Dedicated contract numbers or we can estimate based on instance families; the console will show blended unit cost per route.
01:51 Priya: (scrolling) here is the per-route timeline  the pivot lets you compare routes side by side. you can also drill into a single route and see prompt/response examples, eval traces, and quality metrics like hallucination rate (from your eval sets) if you've connected evaluations.
02:10 Ethan: how are hallucinations measured? we have strict requirements.
02:15 Priya: it's driven off your supplied eval prompts  you tag a route and an eval set, Redwood runs sampling and computes regression metrics; those are surfaced here. caveat is noisy labels can affect the metric, so we recommend curated test sets.
02:29 Jordan: i'll add a link to the eval how-to  Link: https://docs.redwood.ai/console-evals (note: demo link)
02:38 Priya: switching to cost breakdown. the console shows tokens, model tier (like base or tuned), and a breakdown by routing policy  e.g., when requests are routed to a cheaper quantized variant for non-latency-sensitive traffic you'll see cost delta.
02:56 Marta: can you show an example comparison of hosted vs dedicated costs?
03:01 Priya: yes  here's a saved view we prepared for a mid-size retail workload. Hosted per-token unit costs are higher but give you flexibility and no infra commits. Dedicated gives a lower per-token when utilization is above the threshold, we show the breakeven utilization line.
03:22 Priya: (slightly garbled) if you look at the chart, at ~65% sustained utilization Dedicated becomes cheaper for high-throughput routes. for low-volume or bursty routes hosted often wins due to no base commit.
03:39 Lucas: our traffic is spiky  promotions generate bursts. can Redwood autoscale?
03:44 Priya: Dedicated supports burst capacity and configurable autoscale policies; console shows predicted cost during bursts and the expected latency change. we also support hybrid routing  keep critical routes on Dedicated and route burst overflow to Hosted.
03:58 Jordan: that hybrid note is important  many retailers keep inference-critical checkout flows on Dedicated and route search/suggestions to hosted.
04:08 Ethan: security  can you confirm what audit logs and data retention options are shown in the console?
04:15 Priya: yes. console exposes per-request metadata, audit logs, and access events. for Private we provide customer-managed KMS/HSM and full audit log export; for Hosted we retain logs per your data retention policy (configurable). we'll share the SOC2 and ISO artifacts.
04:32 Marta: we need SSO + SAML + role-based access controls.
04:36 Jordan: Redwood supports SSO/SAML, SCIM provisioning, and fine-grained RBAC. we'll attach the security playbook in the follow-up.
04:45 Priya: back to dashboards  one useful widget is the cost waterfall: tokens -> model variant selection -> batching efficiency -> cache hits. you can see how throttling or different batching windows affects unit cost.
05:05 Lucas: batching efficiency  can Redwood show suggested batching config?
05:09 Priya: yes that's in Redwood Optimize. console surfaces recommended batching window and expected latency tradeoff; you can apply suggestions or run A/B tests via the rollout tab.
05:20 Jordan: quick interjection  Link: https://redwood.ai/docs/optimize (demo link)
05:26 Priya: (narration) here's an example where enabling prefix caching reduced token spend 18% on a route that has repeated system prompts. the console lists top candidates for caching.
05:40 Ethan: for our compliance team it's important to see per-route redaction and PII detection. does console show PII hits?
05:47 Priya: we have optional PII detection hooks  hits are tagged and can be redacted before storage; flagged events are visible in the route audit and you can create retention policies per route.
05:59 Marta: can we export the per-route cost report to CSV?
06:03 Priya: yes, export and scheduled reports are supported. we'll also show API endpoints so you can pull the same data programmatically.
06:12 Jordan: i'll note the demo request  Lucas wants an export and a scheduled weekly cost report.
06:17 Lucas: yep thanks.
06:19 Priya: moving on: routing policies  you can define policies based on latency SLO, cost thresholds, region, or tag (e.g., customer_tier). the console shows simulation mode so you can see hypothetical cost and latency before activating.
06:36 Ethan: how granular is per-route? we have routes defined by product_id + intent.
06:42 Priya: console supports arbitrary route keys; many customers use product_id+intent and then aggregate. latency and cost KPIs are computed at that key.
06:50 Marta: about the pilot  we want to run a throughput/latency benchmark for three top routes, simulate Black Friday load. what's involved?
06:58 Priya: typical pilot is 1) ingest sample prompts, 2) Redwood runs a benchmark with your traffic shape in our sandbox or on your Dedicated evaluation pool, 3) we return p50/p95 and cost projections. we recommend a 2-hour window for reproduceable results.
07:16 Jordan: action: Priya will set up the pilot with Lucas; Jordan will send the pricing + sizing.
07:24 Marta: and we'll share top routes + weekly traffic estimates.
07:28 Ethan: any gotchas with VPC or Private? we may need on-prem later.
07:33 Priya: Private deployment is supported; there is an additional ops lead time for on-prem and network setup. console feature parity is near complete but some audit integrations are per-customer. we'll include typical timelines in the follow-up.
07:48 Jordan: competitors  we know you've evaluated other vendors. any specific concerns?
07:52 Marta: we've talked to Anthropic and OpenAI; main questions are cost predictability and control over data.
07:58 Jordan: understood  the console and Optimize tooling are built to show unit economics and give levers to lower cost while keeping quality. we'll include a case study.
08:10 Priya: any remaining questions?
08:13 Ethan: one more  how do rollouts work if we change model version for a route? can we canary?
08:20 Priya: yes you can do canary and A/B with automatic rollback on error or quality regression. console shows the rollout dashboard and recent eval diffs.
08:31 Marta: great, that's helpful. thanks.
08:34 Jordan: ok wrapping: next steps recap: Jordan  pricing deck + dedicated sizing spreadsheet by Mon 12/14; Priya  pilot test plan and scheduling; Marta  top routes and token estimates. we'll follow up with SOC2 docs and a security playbook.
08:51 Ethan: sounds good. thanks everyone.
08:54 Jordan: thanks all, we'll send calendar invites for the pilot. end.
